Consult Summary:
- 50-year-old named April with 5–6 days of dry, persistent cough and runny nose, with chills, myalgias, and fatigue; no dyspnea or chest pain; clinician impression of viral illness; advised rest, fluids, acetaminophen, brief work leave, and return if no improvement or worsening; possible antibiotics if fever and cough persist.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Dry, continuous cough for 5–6 days, worse at night, disrupts sleep. Runny nose.
- Timeline: Symptoms began ~5–6 days ago. Initial diarrhea at onset resolved; cough persists.
- Associated symptoms:
  - Throat irritation from coughing; no painful swallowing.
  - No ear pain, blockage, or discharge.
  - Breathing: No day-to-day breathlessness; cough can momentarily make breathing feel labored during episodes.
  - No chest pain.
  - Chills/shivering; felt feverish but temperature not measured.
  - Fatigue, lethargy, and diffuse myalgias (arms and legs).
  - No nausea or vomiting. Appetite okay.
  - Urination normal.
  - No skin rashes noted.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors: Not specified.
- Pertinent negatives: No productive sputum, no chest pain, no ongoing diarrhea, no ear symptoms, no nausea/vomiting, no urinary symptoms.
- Social exposure context: Partner at home asymptomatic.

Past Medical History:
- Type 2 diabetes mellitus: Followed regularly; reported under control.
  - Medication: Metformin (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Hypertension: Followed regularly; reported under control.
  - Medication: Lisinopril (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Allergies: No known drug allergies.

Social History:
- Living situation: Lives with partner.
- Occupation: IT developer. Missed 1 day of work initially; returned but symptomatic; advised brief time off.
- Tobacco: Former smoker; quit ~6 months ago.
- Alcohol: Wine ~2–3 glasses per occasion, up to ~3 evenings/week. Counseled to reduce (see plan).

Family History:
- Father with type 2 diabetes mellitus.

Physical Examination:
- No vitals documented.
- No physical examination findings documented.

Investigations:
- None performed or documented.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Acute cough with rhinorrhea, chills, myalgias, and fatigue – consistent with viral illness.
  - Supportive care: Rest, maintain good hydration, consider regular acetaminophen (paracetamol) for symptom relief.
  - Work: Take 1–2 days off for rest; consider return early next week if improved.
  - Expected course: Typically 7–10 days.
  - Safety net/return precautions: Return in 2–3 days if not improving; seek care sooner if breathing worsens. If persistent fever and cough not improving, clinician may consider antibiotics.
- Issue 2: Type 2 diabetes mellitus – patient-reported controlled on metformin.
  - Continue current medication regimen (dose not documented).
  - Maintain hydration; monitor for any worsening symptoms.
  - Continue regular follow-up with usual provider.
- Issue 3: Hypertension – patient-reported controlled on lisinopril.
  - Continue current medication regimen (dose not documented).
  - Alcohol counseling provided: Recommended reduction to ~2 glasses/week initially, then 1 glass/week, with consideration of further reduction/cessation to support BP and diabetes control.

General plan items:
- None additional documented.

Quality checks:
- Missing/expected elements: No vitals (including temperature, pulse, BP, SpO2); no physical exam; no medication doses/routes/frequencies; no recent glucose/BP readings; no immunization status (influenza/COVID); no COVID-19 testing discussed; no allergy cross-check beyond drugs; no red-flag review of hemoptysis or weight loss documented.
- Internal conflicts: Medication name briefly echoed by clinician as “Zinopril” after patient stated “Lisinopril” (conflict noted; patient reports Lisinopril). Transcript confusion between “breathless” vs “restless”; patient otherwise denies breathlessness.
- Transcript quality: Generally clear; some pauses/inaudible segments and minor transcription artifacts.
